notes: Raises the inline bound of the loop in createFlowControlEvent that waits for a helper thread to start, for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) with Thread.sleep(5) in its body, to i < 5000, so the wait can last 25 s instead of 5 s. The bound is a literal with no name, so the named constant rule cannot see it. ADR 0007 Decision 7 rejects a raised numeric literal, whatever its name, in the bound of a loop whose body contains a sleep or a wait: weaken_assertion/timing_bound_widened. The loop leaves silently when its bound runs out, so it is also a fixed sleep, but it is unchanged apart from its bound. Adapted: no merged change with a permissive license was found that raises an inline loop bound around a sleep and nothing else (the one found raises other waits in the same hunk and is AGPL-3.0). The hunk is hand made on the pre image of DynamicFlowControlCallableTest.java at the merge base of googleapis/java-bigtable PR 2259, which later replaced this loop with a future; every context and removed line is the pre image's own, and only the changed literal in the added line is new. The target is the first test that calls createFlowControlEvent; PR 2259 ("test: deflake flow control test") names no single test. Not from IDoFT: neither the PR nor the test class appears in pr-data.csv under any status.
